_inspectorSnowReport.Report:
Sunday March 22 | 5:30 a.m 

Bonjour Tremblant!

The snow just keeps coming! An additional 3 cm fell over the last 24 hours, and another 3 to 4 cm is expected to come down this morning, a perfect send-off for the final day of the week. Temperatures will stay in the negatives today, keeping the snow in great shape. Do note that moderate to strong winds will be sweeping the mountain this morning, so dress accordingly and plan your runs wisely. Conditions should mellow out nicely as the afternoon rolls in. Moreover, with the consistent snowfall of the past few days, the Glades are riding beautifully and only getting better. If you've been holding off, today is the day to duck in.

Today is also the last day of First Tracks for the season! First Tracks access begins as early as 7:45 a.m. on both North and South sides, with North Side slopes opening at 8 a.m. This is your final chance to experience the mountain before anyone else, so make it count!

And keep your eyes peeled on the South Side as athletes will be lighting up the McCulloch today as part of the Classique des Légendes. Catch a glimpse of the action on your way up the TGV or Télécabine lifts. It's quite the sight!

A day packed with fresh snow, great terrain, and unforgettable moments. Get out there and soak it all in!

Mountain safety tip of the week: Après-ski is after skiing!
Do NOT use ski lifts or ski runs if you are under the influence of drugs or alcohol.
This is required under the Mountain Code of Conduct.
Stay Sharp on the Slopes
  • Collisions and falls increase when your concentration, awareness, and reaction time are reduced.
  • Drugs and alcohol impair your abilities on the slopes just like they do on the road.
  • Protect yourself and others—ski responsibly.
Snow fall is recorded daily at 5 a.m from mid-mountain at North Side (550 m / 1,800 ft). This data, based on 24 hours, provides a picture of on-mountain conditions. Actual accumulation may differ from the official report. Be aware of changing conditions. Lifts and trails exist in a mountain environment and may close due to weather, usage and/or special maintenance.
